15-1.title: The Roman Republic
15-1.learn:
KEY IDEAS — THE ROMAN REPUBLIC

Rome began on the Italian peninsula and grew into a powerful state. Importantly, Rome started as a REPUBLIC. A republic is a government in which citizens ELECT leaders to make decisions for them, instead of being ruled by a king. (Rome had once had kings, but Romans overthrew them and created the Republic.)

In the Roman Republic, citizens elected leaders, including powerful officials. The most important leaders were the SENATORS, who served in the Senate and helped run the government and make laws. To stop any one person from gaining too much power, Rome created a system with a SEPARATION OF POWERS — power was divided among different leaders and groups. Rome also believed in the RULE OF LAW, meaning everyone had to follow the law. Rome's early laws were written down in the Twelve Tables.

These ideas — electing leaders, separating powers, and the rule of law — later INFLUENCED many governments, including the UNITED STATES. Roman citizens were also expected to take part in government, a responsibility called CIVIC DUTY. Remember: a republic = citizens elect their leaders (Rome's early government).

questions.question: Rome's earliest written laws were known as the what?

questions.question: Which list correctly names Roman ideas that influenced later governments?

questions.question: On which peninsula did Rome begin and grow?

questions.question: What did Romans do to their kings before creating the Republic?

questions.question: Where did Roman senators serve?

questions.question: A student says, 'In my country, citizens vote to choose their lawmakers instead of obeying a king.' Which Roman idea does this match?

15-2.title: The Punic Wars and Roman Expansion
15-2.learn:
KEY IDEAS — THE PUNIC WARS AND ROMAN EXPANSION

As Rome grew stronger, it came into conflict with another powerful trading city, CARTHAGE, located in North Africa. Rome and Carthage fought three long, brutal wars called the PUNIC WARS over control of the Mediterranean Sea and its trade.

The Punic Wars produced one of history's most famous generals: HANNIBAL of Carthage. In a daring move, Hannibal marched his army — including WAR ELEPHANTS — over the snowy Alps mountains to attack Rome from the north. He won several battles and nearly defeated Rome.

In the end, however, ROME WON all three Punic Wars. Rome eventually destroyed the city of Carthage completely. These victories were a huge turning point: they made Rome the MASTER of the Mediterranean, giving it control of valuable land, trade, and resources across the region. Winning the Punic Wars set the stage for Rome to grow from a regional power into a mighty empire that would dominate the ancient Mediterranean world. Remember: Punic Wars = Rome vs. Carthage; Hannibal's elephants; Rome won.

15-3.title: From Republic to Empire
15-3.learn:
KEY IDEAS — FROM REPUBLIC TO EMPIRE

As Rome grew huge and powerful, its REPUBLIC began to struggle. There were problems like fighting between rich and poor, growing armies loyal to their generals, and political violence. In this troubled time, a brilliant general named JULIUS CAESAR rose to power and took control of Rome, ruling almost like a king. Many senators feared he had too much power, so a group of them ASSASSINATED (killed) Caesar in 44 BC.

Caesar's death led to more civil war. In the end, Caesar's adopted heir, OCTAVIAN, defeated his rivals and took power. He took the name AUGUSTUS and became the FIRST EMPEROR of Rome. This change marked the end of the Roman Republic and the beginning of the ROMAN EMPIRE.

Under Augustus, Rome entered a long period of PEACE and stability called the PAX ROMANA, meaning 'Roman Peace,' which lasted about 200 years. The most important change was that POWER shifted from elected leaders (the Republic) to ONE powerful emperor (the Empire). Remember: Republic = elected leaders; Empire = ruled by an emperor. Augustus was Rome's first emperor.

questions.question: Who was Octavian to Julius Caesar?

questions.question: In a republic, who holds the power to choose leaders?

questions.question: In which year was Julius Caesar assassinated?
